# Box plots - Practice Test - Year 10

Attempt all questions and show your working. Suggested time: 30 to 35 minutes.

## Section A: Consolidating (Questions 1-4)

**Question 1**

The number of books read last year by 10 students is shown in order:

3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 11, 12, 14, 15, 18

(a) Find the median.

(b) Find the range.

**Question 2**

The five-number summary for a set of test marks is: minimum $12$, lower quartile $Q_1 = 18$, median $25$, upper quartile $Q_3 = 31$, maximum $40$.

(a) Find the range.

(b) Find the interquartile range (IQR).

**Question 3**

Here are 8 values in order:

2, 4, 7, 9, 12, 13, 17, 20

Find:

(a) the lower quartile $Q_1$

(b) the upper quartile $Q_3$

(c) the interquartile range.

**Question 4**

A box plot shows the waiting times of 60 people at a bus stop. Its five-number summary is: minimum $1$ minute, $Q_1 = 4$ minutes, median $7$ minutes, $Q_3 = 12$ minutes, maximum $20$ minutes.

(a) What percentage of the people waited between 4 and 12 minutes?

(b) Approximately how many people waited more than 7 minutes?

(c) Approximately how many people waited less than 4 minutes?

## Section B: Standard (Questions 5-16)

**Question 5**

The maximum daily temperatures (in $^\circ\text{C}$) in a country town over 12 days were:

21, 18, 25, 30, 19, 23, 27, 22, 17, 24, 29, 26

Find the five-number summary.

**Question 6**

A call centre records how many minutes customers spend on hold. For one day, $Q_1 = 20$ minutes and $Q_3 = 28$ minutes.

A value is an outlier if it is more than $1.5 \times \text{IQR}$ below $Q_1$ or more than $1.5 \times \text{IQR}$ above $Q_3$.

(a) Find the IQR.

(b) Find the lower and upper limits (fences) for outliers.

(c) Which of these waiting times would be outliers: 5, 10, 38, 42?

**Question 7**

The number of push-ups 16 students did in one minute is shown in order:

12, 15, 18, 20, 21, 22, 24, 25, 27, 28, 30, 32, 33, 35, 40, 44

(a) Find the five-number summary.

(b) Show that there are no outliers (use the $1.5 \times \text{IQR}$ rule).

(c) Draw a box plot of the data on a scale from 10 to 50.

**Question 8**

Two Year 10 classes sat the same test, marked out of 50. Their five-number summaries are:

| | Minimum | $Q_1$ | Median | $Q_3$ | Maximum |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Class A | 18 | 28 | 34 | 40 | 48 |
| Class B | 22 | 31 | 36 | 39 | 45 |

(a) Which class has the higher median?

(b) Find the IQR for each class.

(c) Find the range for each class.

(d) Which class had more consistent results? Give a reason.

**Question 9**

The commute times (in minutes) of workers in two suburbs, Northvale and Southbank, are summarised below.

| | Minimum | $Q_1$ | Median | $Q_3$ | Maximum |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Northvale | 10 | 22 | 30 | 38 | 55 |
| Southbank | 15 | 30 | 42 | 50 | 70 |

State whether each statement is true or false.

(a) The median commute in Southbank is 12 minutes longer than in Northvale.

(b) About 75% of Southbank workers commute for 30 minutes or more.

(c) Northvale has the larger interquartile range.

(d) The range of Southbank commute times is 50 minutes.

**Question 10**

For each five-number summary (minimum, $Q_1$, median, $Q_3$, maximum), state whether the data is symmetric, positively skewed or negatively skewed.

(a) 2, 10, 12, 14, 22

(b) 5, 8, 10, 18, 35

(c) 20, 45, 52, 55, 58

**Question 11**

The ages of 16 people at a community gardening session are shown in this stem-and-leaf plot. The stem is the tens digit and the leaf is the units digit, so $1 \mid 5$ means 15.

| Stem | Leaf |
|---|---|
| 1 | 5 8 9 |
| 2 | 0 3 4 7 |
| 3 | 1 2 6 8 |
| 4 | 0 5 9 |
| 5 | 2 6 |

(a) Find the five-number summary.

(b) Find the interquartile range.

(c) Are there any outliers? Show how you decided.

**Question 12**

Twenty households were asked how many pets they have.

| Number of pets | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 3 | 6 | 5 | 4 | 2 |

(a) Find the median.

(b) Find $Q_1$ and $Q_3$.

(c) Find the interquartile range.

**Question 13**

Ten people recorded how many kilometres they cycled on the weekend:

8, 12, 14, 15, 16, 18, 19, 21, 22, 48

(a) Find the five-number summary.

(b) Show that 48 is an outlier.

(c) When this data is drawn as a box plot with outliers shown, where does the upper whisker end, and how is 48 shown?

**Question 14**

The heights (in cm) of 10 tomato seedlings are:

4.2, 5.8, 3.9, 6.5, 5.1, 7.0, 4.8, 5.5, 6.1, 4.5

(a) Find the five-number summary.

(b) Find the interquartile range and the range.

**Question 15**

A box plot shows the times 80 students took to finish an online quiz. The five-number summary is: minimum 12 minutes, $Q_1 = 20$ minutes, median 28 minutes, $Q_3 = 45$ minutes, maximum 60 minutes.

(a) Approximately how many students took more than 45 minutes?

(b) Approximately how many students took between 20 and 28 minutes?

(c) The part of the box to the right of the median is much longer than the part to the left. What does this tell you about the times?

**Question 16**

A consumer group tested how long (in hours) two brands of torch batteries lasted. The five-number summaries are:

| | Minimum | $Q_1$ | Median | $Q_3$ | Maximum |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Brand P | 18 | 22 | 25 | 27 | 30 |
| Brand Q | 21 | 24 | 26 | 27 | 29 |

Which brand would you recommend? Justify your answer using the median and the IQR.

## Section C: Advanced (Questions 17-20)

**Question 17**

Eight values, written in ascending order, are:

4, 6, $x$, 9, 13, $y$, 18, $z$

The lower quartile is 7, the upper quartile is 17 and the range is 20.

(a) Find the values of $x$, $y$ and $z$.

(b) Find the median.

**Question 18**

Twelve Year 10 students at each of two schools recorded how many minutes of exercise they did on one day.

Hilltop: 20, 25, 30, 30, 35, 40, 45, 45, 50, 55, 60, 95

Lakeside: 30, 35, 40, 45, 45, 50, 50, 55, 60, 60, 65, 70

(a) Find the five-number summary for each school.

(b) Show that 95 is an outlier for Hilltop, and that Lakeside has no outliers.

(c) Compare the two distributions, referring to the median and the IQR.

**Question 19**

In one year, 200 houses were sold in a suburb. The sale prices had this five-number summary: minimum \$410 000, $Q_1$ \$620 000, median \$750 000, $Q_3$ \$910 000, maximum \$1 400 000.

(a) Find the interquartile range.

(b) Using the $1.5 \times \text{IQR}$ rule, was the most expensive house an outlier? Show your working.

(c) Approximately how many houses sold for between \$620 000 and \$910 000?

(d) A real estate agent says, "A typical house in this suburb sells for over \$800 000." Use the box plot information to comment on this claim.

**Question 20**

(a) Write down a set of 8 whole numbers that has minimum 2, lower quartile 5, median 10, upper quartile 14 and maximum 20.

(b) Explain why two different data sets can have exactly the same box plot.

# Box plots - Answer Key

**Question 1**

Answer: (a) $10$ ($\frac{9 + 11}{2}$) (b) $15$ ($18 - 3$)

**Question 2**

Answer: (a) $28$ (b) $13$ ($31 - 18$)

**Question 3**

Answer: (a) $5.5$ ($\frac{4 + 7}{2}$) (b) $15$ ($\frac{13 + 17}{2}$) (c) $9.5$

**Question 4**

Answer: (a) $50\%$ (b) about $30$ people (c) about $15$ people

**Question 5**

Answer: minimum $17$, $Q_1 = 20$, median $23.5$, $Q_3 = 26.5$, maximum $30$ (ordered: 17, 18, 19, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, 29, 30)

**Question 6**

Answer: (a) $8$ minutes (b) lower limit $8$, upper limit $40$ ($20 - 12$ and $28 + 12$) (c) $5$ and $42$

**Question 7**

Answer: (a) $12$, $20.5$, $26$, $32.5$, $44$ (b) IQR $= 12$; limits are $20.5 - 18 = 2.5$ and $32.5 + 18 = 50.5$; all values lie between these, so no outliers. (c) Box from $20.5$ to $32.5$ with a line at $26$; whiskers to $12$ and $44$.

**Question 8**

Answer: (a) Class B (b) A: $12$, B: $8$ (c) A: $30$, B: $23$ (d) Class B, because its IQR and range are both smaller, so its marks are less spread out.

**Question 9**

Answer: (a) true (b) true (c) false (Northvale $16$, Southbank $20$) (d) false (it is $55$ minutes)

**Question 10**

Answer: (a) symmetric (b) positively skewed (also accept skewed right) (c) negatively skewed (also accept skewed left)

**Question 11**

Answer: (a) $15$, $21.5$, $31.5$, $42.5$, $56$ (b) $21$ (c) No. Limits are $21.5 - 31.5 = -10$ and $42.5 + 31.5 = 74$; every age lies between them.

**Question 12**

Answer: (a) $2$ (10th and 11th values are both 2) (b) $Q_1 = 1$, $Q_3 = 3$ (c) $2$

**Question 13**

Answer: (a) $8$, $14$, $17$, $21$, $48$ (b) IQR $= 7$; upper limit $= 21 + 10.5 = 31.5$, and $48 > 31.5$ (c) The whisker ends at $22$ (the largest value that is not an outlier) and 48 is shown as a separate point (a dot or cross).

**Question 14**

Answer: (a) $3.9$, $4.5$, $5.3$, $6.1$, $7.0$ (all in cm) (b) IQR $= 1.6 \text{ cm}$, range $= 3.1 \text{ cm}$

**Question 15**

Answer: (a) about $20$ (b) about $20$ (c) The middle-upper 25% of times (28 to 45 minutes) are much more spread out than the middle-lower 25% (20 to 28 minutes); the data is positively skewed.

**Question 16**

Answer: Brand Q. It has the higher median ($26$ hours vs $25$ hours) and the smaller IQR ($3$ vs $5$), so its batteries tend to last longer and more consistently.

**Question 17**

Answer: (a) $x = 8$, $y = 16$, $z = 24$ (from $\frac{6 + x}{2} = 7$, $\frac{y + 18}{2} = 17$, $z - 4 = 20$) (b) $11$

**Question 18**

Answer: (a) Hilltop: $20$, $30$, $42.5$, $52.5$, $95$; Lakeside: $30$, $42.5$, $50$, $60$, $70$ (b) Hilltop IQR $= 22.5$, upper limit $52.5 + 33.75 = 86.25 < 95$. Lakeside IQR $= 17.5$, limits $16.25$ and $86.25$, all values inside. (c) Lakeside has the higher median ($50$ vs $42.5$) and the smaller IQR ($17.5$ vs $22.5$), so Lakeside students tended to exercise more, with less variation.

**Question 19**

Answer: (a) \$290 000 (b) Yes. Upper limit $= 910\,000 + 1.5 \times 290\,000 = 1\,345\,000$, and \$1 400 000 is above this. (c) about $100$ (d) Not supported: the median is \$750 000, so half the houses sold for \$750 000 or less.

**Question 20**

Answer: (a) Any 8 ordered values with smallest 2, largest 20, 2nd + 3rd $= 10$, 4th + 5th $= 20$, 6th + 7th $= 28$; for example 2, 4, 6, 9, 11, 13, 15, 20. (b) A box plot only shows five values (minimum, $Q_1$, median, $Q_3$, maximum), not the individual data, so the other values can change without changing the plot.
check_notes: Every five-number summary, IQR, outlier fence and count recomputed in Python (median-of-halves quartiles); true/false and comparison answers re-read against the tables.
